limitations: Endpoint labels do not prove independent providers or authenticated state.
Fallback handles unavailable reads, never searches for a preferred agreeing quote.
A planning minimum is not enforced by a router; no signing or sending is supported.
No settlement, transfer behavior, gas, MEV, future liquidity or freshness guarantee.
The .example failure is simulated; only one real archived source is available.
Receiver-assigned groups do not authenticate independent upstreams.
A relabeled copied capture can pass an incorrectly trusted receiver policy.
Saved RPC data and endpoint labels are not authenticated state or proof of independent providers.
The caller supplies the block anchor and reference height; no current freshness is measured.
Arithmetic is inherited, not independently proved; coverage is limited to the saved bitmap.
The positive planning minimum is not enforced by a router or receipt.
No token settlement, gas, MEV, future state, signing or sending is modeled.
Provider groups are receiver assertions, not authenticated upstream identities.
Copied evidence relabeled as two approved groups can still pass.
Saved RPC data and endpoint labels are not authenticated state or proof of independent providers.
The caller supplies the block anchor and reference height; no current freshness is measured.
Arithmetic is inherited, not independently proved; coverage is limited to the saved bitmap.
The positive planning minimum is not enforced by a router or receipt.
No token settlement, gas, MEV, future state, signing or sending is modeled.
Recomputed SHA-256 binds bytes to reported hashes; RPC returns and block headers are still unauthenticated.
This is not an Ethereum account proof, code-behavior audit, permission approval or transaction authority.
Only measured standard ERC-20 pairs at this historical block are covered; current state and undiscovered authorizations remain unknown.
Empty balances and empty code never revoke a nonzero allowance; pair exposure bounds overlap per owner.
Proxy targets, delegated code, precompiles, controllers and future execution are not resolved.
A missing spender is not a revocation; it was not rechecked in the after report.
Runtime code hashes describe bytes only, not controller, proxy target or behavior.
Reports cover only active standard ERC-20 spenders already discovered by the caller.
RPC reports are trusted observations, not proofs of chain state or transaction safety.

ZTO.scope: Comparison of supplied proof-backed structural scans only. Runtime entries present on one side mean evidence entered or left this scan, never newly deployed or destroyed code. Site identities include caller address, caller runtime hash, PC and opcode; changed runtime hashes do not reuse site identities. Fewer missing constant-target proofs may expose more unresolved sites. Sites absent from the after scan are not proven resolved or unreachable. Equal scans do not prove complete dependencies, safety, current state or continuous stability. Different heights do not prove common-chain ancestry. Headers, anchors, beacon implementation call results, proxy routing and reachability remain unauthenticated. No transaction approval is emitted.

source_proof.scope: Proofs bind runtime hashes and measured proxy slots to the reconstructed header. Consensus/finality, supplied-anchor authenticity, beacon call results, routing semantics and contract safety are not verified.

result.scope: Raw state/header/runtime proofs at one historical block, joined to locally constant decoded call operands. Root target bytes are identified, not replaced by candidate proxy implementation bytes. Source-path and beacon accounts may satisfy matching operands. Missing proofs remain explicit; unresolved calls and metadata findings remain included. No recursive dependency scan, execution, ABI/source equivalence, current code, consensus, finality, anchor authenticity, safety or permission to transact is established.

result.limits: Matched means only that two provider-reported historical eth_call results equal explicit expected bytes, one with provider-default gas and one with the exact declared gas allowance. This is not gas consumed, an estimate, a minimum gas search, a safe transaction gas limit, authorization or approval. A call may inspect gasleft() and change behavior with its allowance. RPC errors do not establish out-of-gas. No current state, side effects, future execution, ABI correctness or chain/provider authenticity is established. The sender may be a contract, not an available transaction origin. Nothing sent.
result.reason: both calls returned the exact expected bytes
